title: File tools get Bash's reach: denied outside the root unless configured, never in .git, .vscode or .idea (option c, A33)

context.task: Option (c), decided by the author on 2026-10-13, and A33: the write gate lets Edit, MultiEdit, Write and NotebookEdit write anywhere outside the repository and, inside it, the git hooks and configuration and the IDE tasks that Claude Code's sandbox protects from Bash. The design is docs/design/ARRANQUE_PUERTAS.md section 10.

select.heading: 10. La opción (c) y A33: diseño para el contrato
A33 — Las herramientas de ficheros escriben lo que el sandbox protege de `Bash`: git y el IDE

problem: The write gate (tools/hooks/require_boundary_validation.py) lets the four file tools write anything outside the repository: when canonical() returns None the target is skipped, with a valid, an invalid or no configuration. Outside the root that reaches the interpreter's site-packages that the validator loads (A19's residual), ~/.zshrc, ~/.claude/settings.json (the ConfigChange hook applies user settings in the session) and Claude Code's memory, which future sessions load without approval. Inside the root it lets them write .git/hooks/pre-commit (the commit-integrity check the person runs on every commit), .git/config (core.hooksPath, core.fsmonitor, aliases) and .vscode/tasks.json, which the sandbox protects from Bash because they make something run as the person later; none is a governed path, so no receipt is asked (CASES.md, A33: the gate exits 0 on a Write payload to each; Bash under the sandbox gets `operation not permitted`). Bash's reach is set by the sandbox; the file tools have none but the gate's and Claude Code's permission prompt.
decisions: D1 Only the class 1 tools (Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit) change. Class 2 tools keep passing; class 3 tools (MCP and unknown) keep passing outside the root, because the gate cannot tell whether they write and many only read a path (publishing a page, sending a file). That limit is declared in the AGENTS.md change, not here.

D2 New key `writable_outside_root` in .actuarii.json, required like every key: a list, possibly empty, of non-empty strings without duplicates. The schema string stays `actuarii-config/1`: the format is not published yet, and a configuration without the key fails with the existing `missing keys [...]` error, which names it.

D3 An entry is absolute (starts with `/`) or starts with `~/`; `*` stays inside one segment and `**` crosses segments, as in governed_paths; it has no `..`, no backslash, no control character and no other wildcard (`?`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, `***`). Each deviation is a ConfigError naming the entry and the cause.

D4 Matching, in one function of tools/project_config.py next to path_matches (one copy): `~/` is replaced by Path.home() of the process; the leading segments without wildcards are resolved with os.path.realpath, so `/tmp/claude-*/**` covers `/private/tmp/claude-501/...` on macOS; the result is matched with path_matches against the target resolved with Path(...).expanduser().resolve(), links followed. A link inside a covered directory that points outside it is therefore not covered. Matching is case-sensitive after resolution: a different spelling that does not match is denied, the safe direction.

D5 The built-in minimum (no .actuarii.json) has no entries: every class 1 write outside the root is denied. With an invalid configuration a class 1 write outside the root is denied with the configuration error, as inside the root today.

D6 Always denied to class 1 tools inside the root, whatever the configuration and whatever receipt exists: the canonical relative path `.git`, anything under `.git/`, under `.vscode/` or under `.idea/`, as canonical() spells it (so `.GIT/config` on a case-insensitive disk is `.git/config`). The set is fixed in code, not configurable: these are what the sandbox protects from Bash because they make something run as the person later. The check runs before the governance lookup and the receipt lookup.

D7 Denial messages follow the gate's form: `[require_boundary_validation] <resolved path> ...`, naming the rule and its source. Outside the root: file tools write outside the repository only where writable_outside_root of <source> says, and the person may add an entry to .actuarii.json (itself governed). Inside the always-denied set: file tools never write it, no receipt authorizes it, the person edits it.

D8 Values. The installer's example configuration gets two entries: "/tmp/claude-*/*/*/scratchpad/**", the scratchpad of each session and not the rest of /tmp/claude-*, where Claude Code keeps the output of background tasks; and "~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/**", the target's normal Claude Code memory, because the agent's memory is mandatory (author, 2026-10-13). <slug> is the target's resolved absolute path with every character that is not an ASCII letter or digit replaced by `-` (Claude Code's convention: /Users/test/Documents/Actuarii gives -Users-test-Documents-Actuarii); if Claude Code's convention differs, the memory write is denied with the D7 message naming the key, and the person adds the entry. The example configuration therefore depends on the target. examples/traianus/actuarii.json gets the scratchpad entry only. Actuarii's .actuarii.json gets ["/tmp/claude-*/*/*/scratchpad/**", "~/.claude/plans/**"]: its memory is the governed one in .claude/memory/ (docs/PLAN.md, Principios de diseño), so its normal memory stays denied.

D9 Order of edits, because adding a required key invalidates the configuration and an invalid configuration denies every write inside the repository except .actuarii.json: first the tests (they need a valid configuration to be written); then tools/project_config.py (the key, its checks, the matcher); then, immediately, .actuarii.json, which stays editable under a receipt; then the hook, the announcement, the installer and the example. Doing .actuarii.json first would be refused by today's loader (unknown key) and would leave project_config.py unwritable.

D10 Once the hook is changed, it applies to this session at once (hooks are read again on every call): write anything outside the repository, such as the contract file for the verifier under $TMPDIR, with Bash, which the sandbox lets write there, not with Write.

D11 The tests that build the configuration format (AGENTS 6.4) are all listed in files_may_touch: each adds the key. The tests that asserted a class 1 write outside the root passes now assert the denial.

D12 Gates: red-first, each red test seen failing for its stated reason before the change that makes it pass; full-suite, `pytest tests/` exits 0 at the commit; verify-red-green, tools/audit/verify_red_green.py exits 0 on the report.

D13 This contract is launched after the A19-A31-A32 and A20 ones are merged (it touches the same hook, announcement and installer); its base commit is stamped then. The AGENTS.md text of the new rule and its declared limits come in the single AGENTS.md change, not here.

behaviours.statement: tools/project_config.py loads `writable_outside_root` as D2 and D3 say, exposes it on ProjectConfig, and the built-in minimum has none (D5).

A class 1 write whose target resolves outside the root is allowed exactly when an entry covers the resolved target (D4); otherwise the gate exits 2 with the D7 message. With the built-in minimum or an invalid configuration it is denied (D5).

A class 1 write whose canonical target is `.git`, under `.git/`, under `.vscode/` or under `.idea/` exits 2 with the D7 message, before any receipt lookup, even with a recent EXECUTE_SAFE receipt for that exact change and with any configuration state (D6).
Class 2 and class 3 tools behave as today, also outside the root and on .git paths; class 1 writes inside the root outside the D6 set behave as today (receipts, primitives, messages).

The announcement adds, after the list of receipt paths, `  File tools (Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit) write outside the repository only in: <entries joined by ', '>`, or `  File tools (Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit) never write outside the repository` when the list is empty, and `  File tools never write .git, .vscode or .idea`. With an invalid configuration it says that the write gate denies every file-tool write inside the repository, except .actuarii.json under a receipt, and every one outside it.

The installer writes the D8 example configuration for that target, its memory entry included; a target whose existing .actuarii.json equals the example for that target is skipped as today, and one that differs is a conflict as today. A Write into the target's normal memory directory then passes the installed gate.
Actuarii's .actuarii.json and examples/traianus/actuarii.json carry the D8 values and load without error.

tests.must_catch: a configuration that loads without writable_outside_root, or with an entry that is relative, has `..`, a backslash, a control character, an unsupported wildcard or a duplicate; or a valid one that is refused
tests.reason: today the key is unknown and every configuration that has it is refused

tests.must_catch: a class 1 write outside the root that passes without a covering entry, under the built-in minimum or with an invalid configuration; a covered one (absolute, `~/`, `*`, `**`, a prefix through a symbolic link) that is denied; a link inside a covered directory that escapes it and passes
tests.reason: today every class 1 write outside the root passes, and the existing tests assert it

tests.must_catch: a class 1 write to .git/config, .git/hooks/pre-commit, a `.git` file, .vscode/tasks.json or .idea/x that passes, with or without a receipt and in any configuration state, or a case variant that passes on a case-insensitive filesystem
tests.reason: today none of those paths is governed and the gate exits 0 (CASES.md, A33)

tests.must_catch: a change to class 2 or class 3 tools, or to class 1 writes inside the root outside the always-denied set
tests.reason: they already behave as B4 at the base commit and must keep doing so

tests.must_catch: an announcement that does not state where file tools write outside the repository and what they never write inside it, or that misstates the invalid configuration
tests.reason: today the announcement has no such lines

tests.must_catch: an installed or example configuration without the D8 entries, a memory entry with another slug than D8's (including a target path with dots, underscores or spaces), an installed gate that denies a Write into the target's normal memory, or an Actuarii configuration that does not load
tests.reason: today the installer's example has no writable_outside_root

commit_message: fix(puerta): herramientas de ficheros con el alcance de Bash (opción c, A33)
